tellings.difference: This telling states the NICAP founding outright and calls it the first civilian UFO study group; the story's existing telling only mentions the gravitator looking like a saucer.
tellings.link_reason: The telling and the story both have Jesse Michels saying Townsend Brown founded NICAP in the 1950s in the United States, and the story's title names that founding outright. It is the same claim at the same scope.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that a researcher named Townsend Brown built a device he called a gravitator, meant to tap into gravity, and that it looked exactly like a flying saucer. Michels adds that in the 1950s Brown helped form NICAP, the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena, which Michels calls the first civilian group to study UFOs. If true, it would tie early anti-gravity research directly to the start of public UFO investigation.
